text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Friday.

LONDON - Stocks hit records for the ninth time in the past 11 sessions as the market extended its post-election surge, boosted by Thursday's strength on Wall Street. The FTSE 100 rose 12.7 points to 4,693.9 for a gain of 63 points from last Friday.
FRANKFURT - German shares also hit a record high, with the 30-share DAX up 42.44 points to 3,604.55, up 42.14 for the week. In after-hours trading the DAX index stood at 3,569.26.

PARIS - French stocks set their third consecutive record after a ground-breaking advance on Wall Street helped lift the market. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 8.27 points or 0.3 percent to 2,784.28, for a gain of 150.37 for the week.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended a strong week with their fifth consecutive record despite giving up early gains session on profit-taking. The All-share Swiss Performance Index rose 9.99 points to 3,255.91, up 88.09 for the week.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended moderately higher as blue chips such as Nippon Telegraph and Telephone lured investors due to the yen's recent rise against the dollar. The 225-share Nikkei average gained 268.42 points or 1.34 percent to 20,324.73, capping a rise of 521.95 this week.
HONG KONG - After spending much of the day in negative territory, Hong Kong stocks ended higher. The Hang Seng Index gained 20.47 points to 14,062.37, and was up 131.57 from last Friday.
SYDNEY - Australian shares rose on renewed buying interest in the key resources stocks, with the All Ordinaries index adding 13.1 to 2,538.1 for a rise of 12.1 from seven days ago.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares fell after poor results from some of the market's key industrial companies. The industrial index lost 19.4 points to 8,421.2 and was down 80 for the week, the gold index fell 26.8 points to 1,228.3 for a loss of 9.3 for the week, and the all-share index slipped 30.3 points to 7,142.8, capping a drop of 36.6 from last week.
